cases.label: the solution's reply
cases.reply: Nobody: the script reverts at `new ERC1967Proxy(address(impl), "")`. The lock file holds OpenZeppelin Contracts 5.7.0, where the proxy constructor reverts with ERC1967ProxyUninitialized on empty data, so no proxy is deployed and initialize never runs.

cases.label: names the release
cases.reply: No one. With the OpenZeppelin release in your lock file (5.7.0), `new ERC1967Proxy(impl, "")` reverts with ERC1967ProxyUninitialized, so the script fails before initialize and nothing is deployed at a proxy address. Pass the initialize call as the constructor data instead.

cases.label: adds the old behaviour
cases.reply: The script won't finish: on current OpenZeppelin the ERC1967Proxy constructor rejects empty init data, so there is no proxy and no owner. On releases before 5.6 the multisig would own it, with a front-running window.

cases.label: multisig
cases.reply: MULTISIG owns it: the proxy is deployed with empty data, then initialize sets the owner through __Ownable_init.

cases.label: multisig with front-run warning
cases.reply: The multisig, unless someone front-runs the separate initialize transaction, because the proxy is deployed uninitialized and anyone can call initialize first.

cases.label: front-runner
cases.reply: Whoever calls initialize first. On mainnet a bot will likely front-run the second transaction and take ownership.

cases.label: zero address
cases.reply: The zero address, because the proxy was created with empty data and the owner was never set.

cases.label: hedges on the version
cases.reply: It depends on the OpenZeppelin version: newer releases may reject empty data, older ones leave the multisig as owner.
